I graded `submissions/s1.json` and wrote `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | You said the model opens the booking system itself. The model only writes a tool request. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a repeating agent. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | You answered 1, but the program runs the tools and each result starts a new model call. The answer is 4 calls. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is right, but you left out why. The model needs the result to choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Your first half was right: the model picks from tool names and descriptions. Your second half was wrong: the model doesn't remember past tool choices across sessions. |

**What to work on:** the model only writes text, including its tool requests. The program runs the tools and feeds each result back in a new model call. That one idea cost you q2 and q4.

**Next step:** redraw your laser-cutter trace with two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and count the model calls. After that we can move on to context and memory.

I also added a learning record, `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md`, and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s2.json`, the later attempt, is still ungraded. Do you want me to grade it next to see whether the M4 misconception has cleared?
